docs.title: Never let an interested lead go quiet.
docs.text:
The moment someone fills out a form, messages you, or fills in an ad — they get a reply in seconds, and your team gets told immediately. A short morning digest catches anyone who still needs a personal follow-up.

Captures leads from

Typeform Google Forms Meta Lead Ads WhatsApp Email + any other form or ad platform

Replies instantly on

Email WhatsApp SMS

Logs every lead in

Google Sheets Airtable HubSpot + Notion, or your CRM They reach out form, ad, or message → FirstReply replies in seconds, about what they asked → Your team's told Slack, WhatsApp, or email → Logged automatically Sheets, Airtable, your CRM

Every morning: a quick digest flags anyone who still needs a personal follow-up.

Whoever responds first wins the business about 80% of the time — a 2025 survey of nearly 4,000 B2B buyers (6sense B2B Buyer Experience Report). Being first isn't a nice-to-have here, it's most of the outcome.

docs.title: The problem this solves
docs.text:
Whoever responds first usually wins the business, not whoever has the best offer — and most small teams check their leads whenever they get a free moment, which can be hours later:

  • By the time someone gets to it, the lead has often already heard back from a competitor and is talking to them instead, simply because they answered first.
  • A Friday-evening or weekend inquiry sits untouched until Monday, by which point they've moved on.

FirstReply replies the instant someone shows interest, any time of day, so no one's waiting on you — and a short morning digest makes sure a real person still follows up personally on anyone who needs it.

Curious how it actually works under the hood? See how it works · set it up · intake field mapping.

First-responder-wins figure: 6sense's 2025 B2B Buyer Experience Report, survey of ~4,000 B2B buyers. Survey-based, not a controlled study — treat as directional.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: This page goes deep on purpose — it's the proof that the homepage summary is real and tested, not just copy. You don't need to follow all of it to use the result.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  F[Form / Ad / WhatsApp<br/>new lead] -->|webhook + secret| S[Read Settings]
  S --> E[Read existing lead]
  E --> B[Build Response]
  B --> Q[Leads sheet<br/>add or update]
  Q --> C1{Has contact?}
  C1 -->|yes| R1[Reply to lead<br/>email/WhatsApp]
  Q --> C2{Owner contact?}
  C2 -->|yes| R2[Alert owner<br/>WhatsApp/email]
  M[Every morning] --> RD[Read Leads] --> RS[Read Settings] --> DG[Build digest] --> N2[WhatsApp + email to each owner]

All the business rules live in one file, respond.js. build.js copies it into the workflow's Code nodes, so the rules that are tested are the same ones that run.

docs.title: After-hours rule
docs.text: Business hours are Monday–Friday, 9:00–18:00 IST. The reply to the lead goes out immediately, any time — that's the entire point of the workflow. The after-hours check only adds a flag for the owner alert and the morning digest, so a human still follows up personally once the day starts, instead of the lead being forgotten.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
A row is always written, even when something's wrong, and the problem is spelled out in the Flags column and the owner alert:

Flag Meaning Missing: name, what they're asking about Required fields the intake source didn't send No phone or email to reply to Can't send an instant reply — flagged instead of silently failing Arrived after hours – needs personal follow-up Came in outside business hours; the auto-reply still went out No owner set for team Sales Nobody in Settings to alert

docs.title: When the same lead comes in again
docs.text:
The workflow matches on the intake source's lead/response ID.

  • It updates the row rather than creating a duplicate.
  • The Status is never overwritten — a lead marked Contacted stays Contacted.
  • The reply still fires again on an update (e.g. the lead resubmitted with more detail), since that's cheap and better than silently skipping someone who tried again.

docs.title: Morning digest
docs.text:
• Who it covers: leads received in the last 24 hours.
  • What it flags: anyone still New with an open flag — missing info, no contact method, or arrived after hours.
  • Why daily, not weekly: speed-to-lead is an hours-scale problem, not a days-scale one; a weekly cadence (like CloseLoop's) would be too slow here.

docs.title: What's real and what's sample
docs.text:
• Real: the workflow, the rules, and their tests (node respond.test.js).
  • Sample:
  • Every lead is invented. send-test.sh posts a generic lead-shaped sample.
  • The field names in fromIntake() are a starting point for five common sources (see the mapping), not confirmed against any specific client's actual payload yet.
  • WhatsApp replies need a Meta-approved message template before the business can message a new contact first — that's Meta's rule, not a limitation of this workflow. Email is the reliable default until a template's approved.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File What respond.js All rules: intake field mapping, after-hours check, flags, reply text, owner alert, morning digest respond.test.js Fixed-date checks for every rule (node respond.test.js) build.js Builds workflow.json with respond.js inlined into the Code nodes workflow.json Import into n8n (no credentials inside) payloads/, send-test.sh Sample leads and the script that sends them

Capture one real webhook payload per client and adjust fromIntake()

docs.title: Intake field mapping
docs.text:
fromIntake() in respond.js is the one place that needs adjusting per client. Below is the starting map for five common lead sources. Verify against one real webhook payload before going live — this is the fast starting point, not a guarantee, especially for Typeform and Meta where the raw payload is nested.

Our field Typeform Google Forms Meta Lead Ads WhatsApp (inbound) Generic contact form id form_response.token n/a — assign one in the Apps Script step leadgen_id messages[].id whatever the form posts, or generate one name an answer in form_response.answers[], matched by field ref mapped by your Apps Script trigger a field_data entry named full_name contacts[].profile.name name phone an answer with type: "phone_number" same, Apps Script-mapped field_data entry named phone_number messages[].from phone email an answer with type: "email" same, Apps Script-mapped field_data entry named email not applicable email source hardcode "Typeform" hardcode "Google Forms" hardcode "Meta Lead Ad" hardcode "WhatsApp" hardcode to the site name interest the free-text answer, matched by field ref same a custom question's field_data entry messages[].text.body message

Google Forms has no native webhook — the common bridge is a small Apps Script trigger on form submit (or Zapier/Make's Google Forms trigger) that posts a flat JSON object. Whatever keys that script chooses to send are the ones to map here; there's no fixed Google field-name list the way there is for the others.

Typeform and Meta Lead Ads both nest answers in an array rather than flat fields, so fromIntake() needs a small array-search (match by field ref / field name) rather than a direct body.name read — see the comment in respond.js for where that logic goes once you have a real payload.

The same pattern extends to any form tool or ad platform with a webhook or Zapier/Make integration, not just these five.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
You won't run any of this yourself if you hire me for it — this page is here so you (or your own dev team) can see exactly what's involved, and so there's a clean reference when I set it up for your account.

You need Docker and Node 18+. Node is only used for the tests and build.js; n8n itself runs in Docker.

docs.title: 1. Run n8n locally
docs.text:
From the repo folder:

docker run -d --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata -e TZ=Asia/Kolkata -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n -v "$PWD:/files" docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n

Open http://localhost:5678 and create your login.

docs.title: 2. Google Sheet
docs.text:
Create a Sheet with two tabs.

Leads: row 1 headers, in this order:

Received at, Lead ID, Name, Phone, Email, Source, Interest, Owner, Status, Flags
  • Give Status a dropdown: New, Contacted.
  • Format Received at as plain text (Format → Number → Plain text).

Settings: headers Role, Team, Name, WhatsApp, Email:

Role Team Name WhatsApp Email Team Owner Sales name number email Fallback Owner name number email
  • Format the WhatsApp column as plain text, with the country code, e.g. 919800000001.
  • Fallback Owner is used when a lead's team doesn't match any Team Owner row, or when no team is sent at all.

docs.title: 3. Credentials in n8n
docs.text:
• Google Sheets OAuth2 and Gmail OAuth2 (one OAuth client covers both; enable the Sheets, Drive and Gmail APIs):
  • In Google Cloud, create an OAuth client with redirect URI http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback.
  • Add the credential in n8n and sign in.
  • WhatsApp:
  • On developers.facebook.com, create an app and add WhatsApp.
  • On API Setup, add and verify your phone as a recipient. Copy the Phone number ID, the WhatsApp Business Account ID and the access token into an n8n WhatsApp API credential.
  • Before replying to leads on WhatsApp in production, get a message template approved in Meta's WhatsApp Manager — a business can't freely message someone who hasn't messaged first.
  • Webhook secret:
  • Create a Header Auth credential named Intake webhook secret, with header name X-Intake-Secret and a long random value.
  • Copy .env.example to .env and put the same value in it.

docs.title: 4. Build, import, publish
docs.text:
SHEET_ID=<sheet id> WA_PHONE_ID=<phone number id> node build.js

docker exec n8n n8n import:workflow --input=/files/workflow.json && docker exec n8n n8n publish:workflow --id=firstReplyLeads0001 && docker restart n8n

Open the workflow and pick your credentials on the webhook node, every Google Sheets node, both Gmail nodes and both WhatsApp nodes. Then publish. Re-importing resets the credential picks, so pick them again after every rebuild.

docs.title: 5. Try it
docs.text:
./send-test.sh payloads/new-lead.json
Payload What should happen new-lead.json New row in Leads, instant email reply, WhatsApp alert to the Sales owner same file again Still one row; Status stays whatever it was set to missing-fields.json Row flagged Missing: name, what they're asking about, alert starts ⚠ no-contact.json Row flagged No phone or email to reply to; no reply sent, owner still alerted

To see the morning digest now, open Every morning in the editor and click Execute workflow.

To run the rule tests: node respond.test.js should print respond ok.

docs.title: Going live with a real intake source
docs.text:
Route 1: native webhook (recommended).

  1. In the form/ad platform (see the field mapping for where this lives per source), point its webhook or Zapier/Make integration at the production webhook URL, with the header X-Intake-Secret.
  2. n8n must be reachable from the internet: n8n Cloud, or a tunnel.

Route 2: Google Forms, which has no native webhook.

  1. Add a small Apps Script trigger on form submit that posts the response as flat JSON to the webhook URL.
  2. Map whatever keys that script sends in fromIntake().

Before going live: capture one real payload from the client's actual intake source and adjust fromIntake() in respond.js — start from the intake field mapping if they use Typeform, Google Forms, Meta Lead Ads, WhatsApp, or a generic contact form.
